family.tagline: A painter, a developer and one Companion Core in a treehouse.
family.story: Valeria paints and sells prints from the studio loft, and Rafael builds software for clients from the study nook. One Companion Core, on his desk, serves both of their small businesses.

companion.name: Hazel
companion.job: Fills in the framer’s order form in its own browser from Valeria’s list.
companion.limits: Prepares the form only. Valeria checks every field and presses send.

companion.name: Aspen
companion.job: Reads library release pages in its own browser and lists what changed.
companion.limits: Reads and lists only. Rafael decides what gets upgraded.

popup.title: Rafael carries the parcel in
popup.body: A parcel waits at the top of the steps. Rafael carries it to the study nook, where Valeria clears the desk.

popup.title: Valeria slits the tape
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Valeria lifts the Core out and sets it on the desk.

popup.title: Rafael plugs in the cable
popup.body: The cable goes in, and Valeria presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Valeria joins from her phone
popup.body: From the study nook, Valeria opens the Wi-Fi settings on her phone and joins the Core’s own network. Then she picks the home network.

popup.title: Valeria chooses OpenClaw first
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Valeria picks OpenClaw and Inkscape, and Rafael adds Forgejo. The installs carry on while the two of them make breakfast.

beats.capability: an agent with its own browser and tools, running in its own sandbox

popup.title: Hazel says hello
popup.body: A first message goes to the agent Valeria named Hazel. Hazel answers from the Core beside her.

say.speaker: valeria
say.text: Hello, Valeria. I am Hazel. Tell me where to start.

beats.capability: host your own Git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core

popup.title: The invoice script ships
popup.body: A client waits on the invoice script. Rafael tags the release and pushes it to Forgejo. The repository sits on the Core, not on a rented code host.

beats.capability: an agent with its own browser and tools, running in its own sandbox

popup.title: Rafael hands Aspen a reading list
popup.body: Three libraries need a look. Aspen reads each release page in its own browser and writes up what changed. Rafael decides which ones to upgrade.
popup.note: OpenClaw reaches websites over your home internet.

say.speaker: rafael
say.text: Here is what changed. Please read it before you upgrade.

beats.capability: write and run notebooks, code and data in a browser, on your Core

popup.title: Rafael hunts for a missing row
popup.body: A quarterly total comes one row short. Rafael traces it in JupyterLab, then asks the Core’s model through Open WebUI, which answers from the hardware beside him.

beats.capability: connect your apps with workflows, with the data staying on your Core

popup.title: Valeria’s order becomes a packing slip
popup.body: Valeria adds a print order, and a flow Rafael built in n8n writes the packing slip. It runs on the Core, with no connector service in the middle.

beats.capability: merge, split, compress and convert PDFs on your own Core

popup.title: Timesheets travel behind the invoice
popup.body: A month of timesheets must travel behind one invoice. Rafael merges the pages in Stirling-PDF on the Core, then attaches the single file.

beats.capability: control and automate your smart home from one place, locally

popup.title: Rafael links the lamp and TV
popup.body: On Saturday afternoon, the floor lamp’s smart bulb and the wall TV switch together in a scene Rafael built. Home Assistant itself needs no cloud account.

beats.capability: stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Valeria replays a canvas in time-lapse
popup.body: The time-lapse of Valeria’s last canvas plays from Jellyfin on the Core to the wall TV. Rafael asks to see the blue wash again.

beats.capability: track the pantry, shopping lists, recipes, chores and household habits in one place

popup.title: The olive oil reaches the list
popup.body: The olive oil is nearly gone, so Valeria marks it low in Grocy. The shopping list on the Core gains a line, and Rafael adds lemons.

beats.capability: track the pantry, shopping lists, recipes, chores and household habits in one place

popup.title: Recycling and compost swap hands
popup.body: This Sunday, Rafael takes the recycling and Valeria takes the compost. Grocy swaps the two jobs on the chore list, next to the pantry stock.

beats.capability: draw logos, diagrams and line art as vector graphics, in your browser

popup.title: Valeria redraws the sketch
popup.body: A pencil sketch waits on the easel while Valeria traces it in Inkscape. The vector file for the next print edition is kept on the Core.

beats.capability: resize and compress images in the browser

popup.title: Valeria shrinks the canvas photos
popup.body: On a bright morning Valeria shoots the finished canvases, then shrinks each photo in Mazanoke. The app resizes and compresses in her browser, and nothing is uploaded.

beats.capability: run a website or blog on your own Core

popup.title: The print page gets a draft
popup.body: At Valeria’s desk, Rafael builds the print page in WordPress and drops in her shrunken photos. The draft stays on the Core while Valeria reads it through.

beats.capability: an agent with its own browser and tools, running in its own sandbox

popup.title: Valeria checks Hazel’s order form
popup.body: Six prints need frames. Valeria’s agent, Hazel, fills in the framer’s order form in its own browser. Valeria checks each field and presses send herself.
popup.note: OpenClaw reaches websites over your home internet.

beats.capability: the Obsidian note app in your browser; notes stay as local Markdown files

popup.title: The green gets written down
popup.body: Beside the easel, Valeria writes down the green she mixed, in Obsidian. It runs in a browser session, and the note is a plain Markdown file on the Core.

beats.capability: the LibreOffice suite in your browser, saved on your Core

popup.title: Rafael drafts a client proposal
popup.body: Beside the tulip planter, Rafael drafts a client proposal in LibreOffice, in his browser. Valeria reads the first line aloud, and he saves the file to the Core.

beats.capability: plan and map hiking and biking routes from GPX files

popup.title: Friday’s ride gets a route
popup.body: On the bench in the meadow, Valeria loads the lake path’s GPX file into Wanderer and traces Friday’s ride. Rafael adds a boathouse stop before she saves it.

popup.title: One Core up in the branches
popup.body: A painter’s prints, a developer’s code and a shared pantry list sit on one Companion Core.

closing.body: Your drawings, repositories and pantry list can live on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: The Nook has a sleigh bed and no desk item; the Core stands on a desk there. Rafael's desk beats fall back to the Core, and no beat names a monitor or a second screen.
WordPress carries a public-access caveat: loft-shop tells a draft that stays on the Core and never says a visitor can open the page. Remote access is not claimed.
Both companions are OpenClaw (the plan's agent app). nook-aspen and loft-hazel open websites and carry the OpenClaw note; Valeria presses send on the framer's form herself.

Walk: front steps, the Nook with the Core, the hearth room and kitchen on the same level, up to the studio loft, then the tulip planter on the deck and the ground-level bench in the meadow. The lot has planters on decks, no ground garden.
Home Assistant switches a bulb and the TV only (network devices); no Zigbee stick and no energy claim. The kitchen has a counter and a bistro table, never an island.
Extra apps beyond the plan: JupyterLab with Open WebUI in with, n8n, Stirling-PDF, Jellyfin, Obsidian, LibreOffice. Open WebUI is never the beat app, so its ChatGPT chip never appears.
No Companion Memory, no Hermes: nothing here needs the chat-service note. Hello, Valeria's agent line, is the only say beside Aspen's.
garden-ride anchors on the meadow bench, not the roof-terrace umbrella table. loft-shop anchors on the loft desk, since the bedroom role alone picks the Tree Bedroom. Mazanoke claims no storage.
